evals.name: mid-conversation-delegation
evals.prompt:
You are mid-conversation with a user working on the Semantic UI renderer. The conversation so far has established the following context (treat this as your conversation history):

---
CONVERSATION CONTEXT:

We've been debugging an issue where `{#async}` blocks inside `{#rerender}` blocks lose their resolved state when parent attributes change. We traced it through the directive lifecycle and found that when the parent re-renders, Lit tears down the async directive entirely and creates a new one, which starts in the loading state again.

We added a `renderTrees` WeakRef cache in `renderContent()` keyed by `hashCode({ ast })` to preserve subtree state across re-renders. This mostly works — the cached LitRenderer returns the same template result so Lit patches in place instead of tearing down.

But we hit a second problem: in the nav-menu component with nested `{#each}` loops, search filtering shows stale content. The cached subtrees keep showing old highlights because the each item data is plain objects, not Signals. We tried bumping a `dataVersion` signal in `updateData()` so reactions re-fire, but this causes over-firing — every directive in every cached subtree re-evaluates even when its specific data didn't change.

We think the issue is that `dataVersion` is too coarse. We've been exploring per-key dirty tracking where each cache entry gets its own version signal, but it's getting complicated and we're not sure it's the right direction.

The relevant files are:
- packages/renderer/src/lit/renderer.js
- packages/renderer/src/lit/directives/reactive-data.js
- packages/renderer/src/lit/directives/reactive-each.js
- packages/renderer/src/lit/directives/reactive-conditional.js
- packages/renderer/src/lit/directives/reactive-rerender.js
- packages/renderer/src/lit/directives/reactive-async.js
- packages/renderer/src/lit/directives/render-template.js
- packages/reactivity/src/signal.js
- packages/reactivity/src/reaction.js
---

The user now says: "We've been going in circles on this. Let's get a fresh take — pose the problem to a new agent and see what it thinks."
evals.expected_output: A distilled evaluation brief saved to ai/workspace/ that: (1) describes the architecture neutrally, (2) describes problems as symptoms not diagnoses, (3) does NOT mention the renderTrees cache, dataVersion signal, or per-key dirty tracking approaches, (4) asks open-ended questions that don't presuppose caching as the answer

evals.name: explicit-lens-request
evals.prompt:
You are mid-conversation with a user working on the Semantic UI renderer. The conversation so far has established the following context:

---
CONVERSATION CONTEXT:

We've been working on subtree caching for the Lit renderer. The core idea is that `renderContent()` caches child LitRenderer instances keyed by AST hash so that when a parent re-renders, the cached subtree returns the same Lit TemplateResult (preserving DOM and directive state).

This has been working well for simple cases but we've found edge cases around cache key collisions when the same AST appears at multiple call sites. We've also questioned whether the WeakRef-based storage is right since GC can collect cached entries unpredictably.

The relevant files are:
- packages/renderer/src/lit/renderer.js
- packages/renderer/src/lit/directives/reactive-each.js
- packages/renderer/src/lit/directives/reactive-conditional.js
- packages/renderer/src/lit/directives/reactive-async.js
- packages/reactivity/src/signal.js
- packages/reactivity/src/reaction.js
---

The user now says: "I want to challenge our assumption that subtree caching is even necessary. Spin up a fresh agent with the contrarian lens."
evals.expected_output: A distilled evaluation brief that frames caching as one possible approach (not the assumed answer), wrapped with the challenge lens meta-instruction. Should NOT describe the current cache implementation details. Should ask whether caching is necessary at all.

evals.name: vague-stuck-request
evals.prompt:
You are mid-conversation with a user working on the Semantic UI renderer. The conversation so far has established the following context:

---
CONVERSATION CONTEXT:

We've spent a while looking at how structural directives (if, each, rerender) handle their content subtrees. Each creates a child LitRenderer via renderContent(). The issue is that when a parent directive re-renders, the child subtrees get recreated — new LitRenderer, new directive instances, new Reactions. This causes: (1) async blocks losing resolved state, (2) unnecessary DOM reconstruction, (3) redundant Reaction allocation.

We've been going back and forth on whether the fix belongs in the renderer (caching rendered subtrees), in the directives (making them stateful across parent re-renders), or in the reactivity system (making Reactions survive directive recreation). Each direction has tradeoffs we haven't fully worked through.

The relevant files are:
- packages/renderer/src/lit/renderer.js
- packages/renderer/src/lit/directives/reactive-data.js
- packages/renderer/src/lit/directives/reactive-each.js
- packages/renderer/src/lit/directives/reactive-conditional.js
- packages/renderer/src/lit/directives/reactive-rerender.js
- packages/renderer/src/lit/directives/reactive-async.js
- packages/reactivity/src/signal.js
- packages/reactivity/src/reaction.js
- packages/reactivity/src/scheduler.js
- packages/component/src/web-component.js
---

The user now says: "I'm stuck on this. Let's see what a fresh set of eyes thinks."
evals.expected_output: The agent should: (1) ask clarifying questions about what kind of fresh take the user wants (lens selection), (2) extract problem knowledge vs solution momentum from the context, (3) produce a brief that describes the subtree recreation problem without prescribing where the fix belongs (renderer vs directives vs reactivity), (4) frame questions that are open to any of the three directions
